islam.title: Sharing Jesus with a Muslim friend
islam.intro: Not to win an argument. To help a real person meet the real Jesus, with gentleness (2 Timothy 2:24–25). Built from the largest study of Muslim conversions ever done, and from ministries with decades in this work.
islam.html:
The invitation to work toward
You, once trust is real

"Would you read one Gospel with me? Luke. The Quran itself says to judge by the Injil."

Quran 5:47 commands it. Quran 10:94 sends doubters to the people who read the Scripture. You are asking your friend to do what their own book says.

What brought ex-Muslims to Christ: the Woodberry findings, ranked
1

The lifestyle and love of the Christians they knew

The top-ranked factor, ahead of every argument. Love inside Christian marriages. Love for enemies. Plain honesty. A Christian who stayed. Nabeel Qureshi and David Wood argued for four years and stayed friends the whole way through: a friend both openly convinced and always there. Most Muslims never have one close Christian friend. Be the first.

2

Reading the Bible, especially the Sermon on the Mount

They are taught it is corrupt, so reading it is the shock. Mosab Hassan Yousef, son of a Hamas founder, put it this way: "When I read love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, I was thunderstruck. This was the message I had been searching for all my life."

3

The character of Jesus, next to their own sources

Mark Gabriel had the whole Quran memorized and taught at Al-Azhar. His doubts began inside the texts, not outside them. What moved him was studying Jesus and Muhammad side by side.

4

Dreams of Jesus, handled factually

Surveys keep finding that 25 to 33 percent of Muslim-background believers report a dream of Jesus before they converted. The pattern is steady. The dream opens the door, and a Bible or a Christian walks through it. Ask gently: "Have you ever had a dream about Jesus?" Many have, and have told nobody.

5

Assurance, against the scales

Converts worn out by earning name this as the thing that decided it. A person can know they are forgiven (1 John 5:13). The scales never offer that.

The method

Never mock Muhammad or the Quran

Honor and shame are the frame here, not guilt. An insult to the Prophet attacks their family, their identity and their community. It triggers the honor-defense reflex and ends the conversation for good. In some settings it can put them in danger. Honest questions about Muhammad are fair. Contempt never is.

Hospitality is the master key

Eating together is the trust currency of Muslim culture. Accept invitations to iftar. Host them back, with no pork and no alcohol. Return the welcome at Christmas and Easter. Most real work with Muslims happens over meals in homes, not in debates.

Use the Quran as a door, never as an authority

"Your own book says striking things about Isa. Have you seen them?" is a fair opener. Then get to the Bible quickly and stay there.

Learn their vocabulary

Isa al-Masih, Injil, Tawrat, Zabur. Using the words signals respect. But define sin, salvation and Son of God before you argue about them.

Tell the gospel in honor and shame

The sin of Adam brought shame, hiding and exile. Jesus bore our shame in public, despising the shame (Hebrews 12:2), so God could cover us, clean us and seat us as his children with honor. Luke 15:22 has the robe, the ring and the feast. This frame lands where courtroom language does not.

Debate and friendship are different tools

Debate videos reach doubters watching alone at two in the morning. They are not a script for the face of your neighbor. What breaks certainty rarely makes disciples on its own. Relationships do.

Never use the weak arguments

This site marks the popular claims that are false or overclaimed. Repeating one hands the other side an easy win and discredits every true argument you made.

Expect years, and pray

Qureshi took four years. Abdu Murray took nine, from being persuaded to saying so out loud, because the cost is so high. This is farming, not harvesting.

How it actually goes

Of about 750 former Muslims surveyed, the top reason they followed Jesus was the lifestyle and love of the Christians they knew. Not arguments.

— Woodberry, Shubin and Marks, Why Muslims Follow Jesus (Fuller Seminary study, Christianity Today, 2007).

The seven objections you will hear

  1. The Bible is corrupted. The flagship, and everything rests on it. The answer has two halves. The Quran endorses the Bible of the day of Muhammad (10:94; 5:47; 5:68; 6:115). The manuscripts prove that Bible is ours: the Dead Sea Scrolls, and Sinaiticus. Ask: "Corrupted before Muhammad? Then why does the Quran endorse it? Corrupted after? Then why do the pre-Islamic manuscripts match ours?"
  2. Jesus never said he was God. Show what he did claim. He forgave sins in his own person (Mark 2:5–7). At his trial he made the Daniel 7 claim that got him condemned for blasphemy (Mark 14:61–64). He accepted the worship of Thomas (John 20:28). He said before Abraham was, I AM (John 8:58). Ask why he was executed for blasphemy.
  3. The Trinity is three gods. Clear the ground first. What the Quran attacks is Allah, Jesus and Mary (5:116). That is tritheism, and Christians condemn it too. One God (Deuteronomy 6:4), three persons: one what, three whos. The Quran itself calls Jesus the Word of God and a Spirit from him (4:171). Were the Word and the Spirit of God ever separate from God?
  4. Paul invented Christianity. The resurrection creed Paul received (1 Corinthians 15:3–8) dates to within a few years of the cross. Peter, James and John endorsed his gospel (Galatians 2:9). If Paul hijacked it, why did the eyewitnesses die for the same message?
  5. Muhammad is the Paraclete of John 14. Read the passage together. The Comforter is the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot see, who would be in the disciples then living (14:17), sent in the name of Jesus (14:26). Muhammad was a visible man born five hundred years later.
  6. The Bible names Muhammad in Song of Songs 5:16. The Hebrew word machmad means lovely, or desirable. It appears about thirteen times in the Old Testament, including of things plundered and destroyed. In context a bride is praising the kisses of her husband. A sound-alike is not a name.
  7. The Gospel of Barnabas is the true gospel. It is a demonstrated forgery from the fourteenth to the sixteenth century: a medieval Jubilee reference, wine casks, quotations from Dante. It also contradicts the Quran, because it denies that Jesus is the Messiah. Most Muslim scholars concede that it is not authentic.

Count the cost, and never out a seeker

Leaving Islam is a crime in about seventeen countries and carries the death penalty in roughly a dozen. In the West the cost is disownment, expulsion, broken engagements, and in extreme cases violence. A convert may lose their family entirely. So never out a Muslim seeker. Not to their family, not on social media, not in a group prayer text. Let them control who knows. Do not run tests with pork or alcohol, because eating bacon proves nothing about faith in Christ (Romans 14). Respect gender lines: men witness to men, women to women. Time baptism wisely. It is the public act that triggers the consequences. And when someone does come to Christ, the church has to become their family in practice, with meals, holidays and help finding a home. Otherwise they drift back, not from doubt but from loneliness. Say it early and often: "I know what this could cost you. I am not going anywhere either way."

Seven bridges, in words they already use

  1. The resume of Isa, to the Word made flesh. Word of Allah, Spirit from him, Messiah, born of a virgin, sinless, alive, returning (3:45–49; 4:171). Ask whose resume that is, and why not read everything this one said. Then John 1:1–14.
  2. Eid al-Adha, to the Lamb of God. "We ransomed him with a great sacrifice" (37:107). Ask what the ram was pointing to, and why a ransom at all. Then Genesis 22:8, John 1:29 and Mark 10:45.
  3. The scales, to assurance. Quran 23:102–103 next to 1 John 5:13. Ask: "Are you sure your good outweighs your bad? Would you want to be sure?"
  4. The ninety-nine names, to the one that is missing. The missing name is Father. Master and slave, or Abba. In Luke 15 the father runs, which costs him honor to do. Then Romans 8:15.
  5. The Zabur, to Psalm 22. The Quran affirms the Psalms (4:163). Read Psalm 22: pierced hands, divided garments, a thousand years early. Then read Matthew 27. The crucifixion the Quran denies in one late verse is described in a book it endorses.
  6. Shame, to honor. Jesus bore shame in public to cover ours and to seat us with honor (Hebrews 12:2). In 1 Peter 2:6, whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.
  7. Quran 10:94, to permission to read. Their own book tells doubters to consult the people who read the Book. Offer to read Luke together, one chapter at a time. Nearly every conversion story runs through an open Bible.
